relaxation training and guided imaging improved mood, quality of life, and coping strategy in women undergoing primary chemotherapy for breast cancer, without increasing clinically significant mood disturbance, and that imagery was correlated with clinical response to treatment.
relaxation training combined with guided imagery is associated with a reduction in emotional suppression and improved mood and quality of live.

the experimental group were significantly more relaxed and easy-going during the study, had better quality of life (Global Self-assessments and Rotterdam Symptom Checklists) and less emotional suppression (Courauld Emotional Control Scale) and had higher imagery ratings, which were correlated with clinical responses to chemotherapy.

the development and testing of interventions to improve quality of and response to primary therapy for breast cancer.
the psychological, clinical and pathological impact of a simple intervention (relaxation training combined with guided imagery) during primary chemotherapy for women with breast cancer.
the psychological, clinical and pathological consequences of relaxation training combined with guided imagery during primary breast cancer chemotherapy.
